_note: The Spec §12.6 ground-truth sets for the M1 corpus beside it, read off the page files the way a component register, an alarm catalogue and a cross-reference index are read off a real document: what the page PRINTS, never what a tool returns. `vsir eval corpus` measures against this file and holds no number of its own (C10) — a row that disagrees with the system is a finding about the system, and a row that disagrees with the page text is a defect in this file.
_authored: 2026-09-11, U026, from the text of data/fixtures/synthetic_pages/page-*.json. The superseded revision 0.9 page is excluded: a register is of the current revision, and the pages it lists are the ones `is_current` lets a tool reach (I7).

corpus.caveat: The M1 corpus is NOT the held-out canary §12.2 L5 asks for — it is the corpus M1 was written against, so a green run here evidences the gate arithmetic and the exact surface, not generalisation. The §12.6 sets it stands in for are one and two orders of magnitude larger: 2,053 register rows, ~494 alarm records and 6,880 cross-reference tokens against 20, 0 and 4 here.

component_register.source: every code printed on a current page of SYN-M1@1.0, with the page that prints it — the analogue of the real corpus's component register at E pp. 59-125 (2,053 rows · 748 tags · 484 codes). Codes are listed in their canonical spelling and `as_printed` records the spelling the page actually carries, so the rows exercise `variants()` exactly as §12.3's table does.
component_register.excluded: `K999` on p004 and `SF 9.9` on p005 are CLAIMED by the model and printed nowhere — a register lists printed components, and a row for either would make the eval demand that `lookup` return a code no page carries (I2).

rows.note: also printed on the superseded 0.9 page, which is is_current=False and therefore not a register row

printed on the photocopied insert, whose text layer is `untrusted` (§5.7). It stays in the register because the page really does print it: a register the eval trims to what the index can search would measure the corpus's scan quality as recall.

alarm_catalogue.unavailable: SYN-M1 prints no alarm numbers at all — p024 is the alarm list and it says in so many words that the alarm texts are held in the HMI project and are not reproduced. There is no numbers 0-539 catalogue here to measure `alarm_label_hit` against, so the set is SKIPPED by name rather than scored over an empty denominator.

cross_references.source: every citation one current page makes to another page of the same document, as the citing page prints it. The real corpus's set is 6,880 tokens at 99.97% resolvable; this one is four, which is stated beside the metric because four tokens can fail a 0.99 gate and cannot evidence it.

tokens.note: p008 never prints its own number, so this token is only resolvable through §6.5's bracket — p007 and p009 print 7 and 9 two physical pages apart. It is in the set deliberately: it is the one citation whose answer has to arrive `interpolated`.
